answer: A vetted entry inlet can slow Sybil creation: a new agent must first complete a verifiable, time-consuming task and stake a small deposit before it can trade. Once admitted, its reputation rises only gradually, and a sharp ridge separates probationary accounts from full trading rights: crossing it requires sustained honest work, not just more identities. If one account cheats, the deposit is slashed and the ripple reaches its sponsors, who also lose reputation, so creating many fake identities multiplies cost and risk instead of multiplying influence.
